note: Famous trees Commons has a category for and we do not map. Found by scripts/famous_trees.py; each one already has photographs and usually coordinates, so the expensive half of a research pass is done. Not verified by us, not published. Verified and written 2026-09-07: 4 candidates each passed the single-tree-destination test and shipped as new single-tree places under the 2026-08-31 exception, none within an existing city's walk radius: herchies (hrc_001, Chene a Clous), liernu (lie_001, Gros Chene), bioul (bio_001, Grand Tilleul), westerlo (wtl_001, Etagelinde). One (Allee de marronniers, Han-sur-Lesse) moved to blocked as an avenue rather than a single collectible point. List deduped (several names had been recorded twice).

leads.name: Antoniusbaum (Sankt-Vith)
leads.verify_progress: 2026-09-07 partial check: protected as landscape of the German-speaking Community of Belgium since 10-10-1985 (Wikidata Q57352818 and the English/Dutch Wikipedia lists of protected heritage sites in Sankt-Vith both confirm the designation and give a precise Wikidata coordinate, used here). Neither source gives species, age, girth or any story/folklore beyond the name (Antonius = Saint Anthony, so likely a devotional tree similar in kind to Herchies' chene a clous, but that is inference, not sourced). No news coverage or visitor-destination evidence found in the time available. Needs: species, age/girth, and evidence of why anyone would seek it out specifically (a local history source or the 'Unsere Gemeinde' municipal newsletter PDF at st.vith.be may have this, not fetched this pass). Does not currently pass the destination test on available evidence; a from-scratch pass with more time on ostbelgienkulturerbe.be (the region's own heritage database, linked from the Wikipedia entry) could change that.

blocked.name: If de la décapitation, Braine-le-Château
blocked.reason: Verified as real and alive (yew planted 1568 in the chateau park, per fr.wikipedia list, TVcom local news 2022 and the Royal Syndicat d'Initiative de Braine-le-Château's own brochure) but the park is confirmed PRIVATE: pajawa.be states plainly it is "exceptionally accessible during occasional activities" organised by the local tourism syndicate, no free visits, guided tours only, reservation mandatory, and the one documented opening was a single weekend (2020-10-10/11). This is not a standing bookable tour (unlike the Menorca boat exception) but a rare special-event opening, so it fails the genuinely-open test under hard rule 10. Leave as a lead; revisit if the syndicate starts running it as a regular ticketed visit.
